result.pr_title: fontforge: decode quoted glyph names; do not emit aalt-only lookups as feature prefixes
result.pr_body:
> **Note**: This post was generated by an AI agent (Claude) working under the guidance of
> @felipesanches, but submitted **without human review**. @felipesanches himself would
> still need to participate in the PR thread if he wants to contribute to the review.

Two fixes to the FontForge (.sfd) reader; no new flags.

- Quoted glyph names: FontForge quotes a `StartChar:` name only when it has a character other than printable ASCII, tab, CR or LF, and writes it in its modified UTF-7 (`SFDDumpCharStartingMarker` and `SFDGetChar` in sfd.c), the encoding the reader already decodes for subtable, lookup, class and nameid strings. A quoted name is now trimmed, unquoted and decoded, so `"C+AJIA-rculo0"` followed by a space becomes `C`, U+0092, `rculo0`; an unquoted name stays literal, `+` included.
- aalt-only lookups: a lookup registered only to `aalt` already has its single and alternate substitutions inlined into the aalt feature, so it is no longer also emitted as a named feature prefix that nothing references. A lookup that a chain context calls by name keeps its definition.

Tests: 4 new unit tests in convertors/fontforge.rs. `cargo test -p babelfont --no-fail-fast`: 201 passed, 11 failed; upstream/main 6ab2312: 197 passed, the same 11 failed (the robocjk and decomposecomponentreferences tests that load the untracked noto-cjk-varco/notosanscjksc.rcjk fixture). Integration tests 7 passed and doc-tests 4 passed, 1 ignored, on both. `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean; `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo clippy -p babelfont --all-targets --features cli`: 0 warnings.

result.pr_title: Add opt-in filters for the OS/2 and post values FontForge's exporter computes
result.pr_body:
> **Note**: This post was generated by an AI agent (Claude) working under the guidance of
> @felipesanches, but submitted **without human review**. @felipesanches himself would
> still need to participate in the PR thread if he wants to contribute to the review.

Three opt-in filters for the OS/2 and post values FontForge's TTF exporter computes. `--fontforge-os2-defaults` fills the x-height, cap height and PANOSE the source does not state. It also computes the ten sub/superscript and strikeout values as a group when the source has no OS2SubXSize, replacing any stated without it, as FontForge does. `--fontforge-height-glyph-count-mean` fills the x-height and cap height the source does not state. `--fontforge-underline-position` converts the UnderlinePosition the source states.

- `--fontforge-underline-position`: FontForge's UnderlinePosition is the underline's centre, and post.underlinePosition is its top. The filter applies `dumppost()`'s rule up to tag 20170731: position - thickness/2 in real arithmetic, truncated towards zero. FontForge reversed the sign in commit 9f667c9c (fontforge/fontforge#3389, first in tag 20190317), so the flag is for a binary exported by an older FontForge, whatever the export date. The SFD reader parses both values as integers and drops a fractional one, which FontForge reads as a real.
- `--fontforge-os2-defaults`, sub/superscript and strikeout: when the source has no OS2SubXSize (FontForge's `subsuper_set`), all ten come from `SFDefaultOS2SubSuper` (tottf.c). The x offsets are derived from the y offsets already truncated to 16 bits. They use the italic angle as the reader holds it, rounded to a whole degree.
- `--fontforge-os2-defaults`, PANOSE: as `SFDefaultOS2Info` computes it. `OS2WeightCheck` sets byte 2 from the Weight: name and then from the FontName. "script" in the FontName (without "sans") sets byte 0 to 3. FontName width words set byte 3, and one shared advance (`CIDOneWidth`) sets it to 9.
- `--fontforge-os2-defaults`, x-height and cap height: each one the source does not state, computed as `setos2` computes it from `SFXHeight`/`SFCapHeight` (`SFStandardHeight`, splinefont.c). `setos2` writes the two only at OS/2 version 2 or later. A TrueType export gets that only from OS2Version, OS2_UseTypoMetrics or OS2_WeightWidthSlopeOnly. For a version-1 export, the filled values are FontForge's estimate, not values found in the binary.
- `--fontforge-height-glyph-count-mean`: the x-height and cap height as a FontForge built before 2012-05-14 (commit 4d34d21ef866) computed them: the sum of the distinct round or pointed tops divided by the glyph count. Run it before `--fontforge-os2-defaults`.

Not modelled, and documented in the rustdoc: a source with none of the lines that set FontForge's `pfmset` (PfmFamily, TTFWeight/PfmWeight, TTFWidth, LineGap, VLineGap). From such a source, FontForge also recomputes a stated PANOSE, sub/superscript group, x-height and cap height, and derives the weight and width classes. The filter keeps the stated values. FontForge's Font Info dialog sets `pfmset` whenever it stores any of those values, so only sources edited by hand or written by another tool are affected.

Independent of #90. With #90, the underline, strikeout and sub/superscript values also reach a .glyphs output as the custom parameters compilers read. The branch merges cleanly with #90 and with the companion FontForge source-fidelity and reader-fix PRs.

Tests: 32 new unit tests (5 underline, 17 OS/2 defaults, 9 standard height, 1 glyph-count mean). `cargo test -p babelfont`: 229 passed, 11 failed. On upstream/main 6ab2312: 197 passed, and the same 11 failed (the robocjk and decomposecomponentreferences tests that load the untracked noto-cjk-varco/notosanscjksc.rcjk fixture). Integration 7/7 and doc-tests 4 passed (1 ignored) on both. `cargo fmt --all -- --check` is clean. `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo clippy -p babelfont --all-targets --features cli` give 0 warnings on every commit of the branch.

result.pr_title: Add opt-in filters for converting FontForge sources
result.pr_body:
> **Note**: This post was generated by an AI agent (Claude) working under the guidance of
> @felipesanches, but submitted **without human review**. @felipesanches himself would
> still need to participate in the PR thread if he wants to contribute to the review.

Five opt-in filters for converting a FontForge source, and one CLI change.

- `--drop-alternate-unicodes`: drop the plain AltUni2 alternate codepoints and keep each glyph's Encoding codepoint, for a target cmap that does not carry the alternates, such as a binary built without them. FontForge's own TTF export does map them, whatever the encoding (`NeedsUCS2Table()` in tottf.c; for a Unicode encoding, `SFD_DoAltUnis()` in sfd.c adds them to the encoding map first; the same in 20120731 and 20230101). It works the other way from `--add-legacy-duplicate-cmap`, which maps a fixed set of such codepoints onto glyphs found by name. Variation sequences are untouched; a glyph with no Encoding codepoint keeps its first one.
- `--reverse-path-direction`: reverse every closed contour; the counterpart to `--correct-path-direction` for a font whose mixed contour directions are meant to be kept.
- `--keep-source-glyph-names`: set the Glyphs custom parameter "Don't use Production Names", so a later compile keeps the glyph names the source states, as FontForge's TTF export does (`dumppost()` in tottf.c). A .glyphs, .glyphspackage or .babelfont output carries the parameter; a UFO or designspace output does not.
- `--keep-source-advances`: record an uncategorised glyph with a non-zero advance as a base, so a compiler does not zero its advance as a mark by its name. Run `--infer-mark-category` first.
- `--snap-component-transforms`: in a glyph made only of components, read a component scale within 1.5 F2Dot14 steps of an integer as that integer, and round each component offset with rint, ties to even, as `dumpcomposite()` in tottf.c does. It touches only a glyph that FontForge exports as a TrueType composite (`IsTTFRefable()`: no contours, and every 2x2 matrix entry in [-2, 1.999939]). FontForge writes any other glyph as a simple glyph: it applies each component's transform as it stands and rounds the points, as a compiler that decomposes the component does, so the filter leaves it alone. A FontForge source may carry a mirror as -0.999939 (-16383/16384 to six digits), which `put2d14()` exports as -1. The scale rule is not `put2d14()`'s floor: FontForge exports +0.999939 as 16383/16384, which this filter reads as 1. A scale near 2 is left as it is, since F2Dot14 cannot hold 2. The same in 20120731 and 20230101.
- CLI (not opt-in): when compiling a TTF, `babelfont` now honours a "Don't use Production Names" custom parameter that is enabled and set to 1 (a number or a string), so a .glyphs source that already carries it compiles without production names. A disabled parameter, or one set to 0, changes nothing.

In `--help`, `--drop-alternate-unicodes` sits under "Filters for subsetting fonts", `--reverse-path-direction` next to `--correct-path-direction` and `--snap-component-transforms` next to `--decompose-components` under "Filters for manipulating outlines", and the two keep-source filters under a new heading, "Filters for keeping what the source states". This PR merges cleanly with each of the companion FontForge reader-fixes and OS/2-defaults PRs.

Tests: 16 new unit tests. `cargo test -p babelfont --no-fail-fast`: 213 passed, 11 failed; upstream/main 6ab2312: 197 passed, 11 failed (the same 11 failures: the robocjk and decomposecomponentreferences tests that load the untracked noto-cjk-varco/notosanscjksc.rcjk fixture). Integration 7/7 and doc-tests 4 passed, 1 ignored, on both. On every commit, `cargo fmt --all -- --check` is clean, and `cargo clippy -p babelfont --all-targets --features cli` and `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` give no warnings; at the tip, `cargo clippy --all-targets` gives none either.

**glyphs-reader-1.0.0.** as_i64 parses a Plist::String (plist.rs:222-228). as_bool is `as_i64 == 1` (font.rs:942-944). Disabled parameters are skipped (font.rs:1159).

issues.where: babelfont/src/filters/snapcomponenttransforms.rs:84-103 (apply loop), rustdoc :22-29; PR body bullet --snap-component-transforms ('It touches only a glyph that FontForge exports as a TrueType composite')
issues.what: The composite check looks only at a layer's own shapes, not at whether FontForge exports that layer. FontForge writes only gi->layer, which is ly_fore by default (IsTTFRefable(sc, gi->layer), tottf.c 2012:1515, 2023:1478). It never writes the Back layer or extra layers. The SFD reader turns those into babelfont layers: Back becomes is_background=true, and `Layer: 2` becomes AssociatedWithMaster with is_background=false. The filter snaps whichever of them hold only components. I checked this with the HEAD binary. In an SFD glyph whose Fore layer has a contour and whose Back layer has `Refer: 0 65 N -0.999939 0 0 1 855.948 0.5 2`, `babelfont bg.sfd out.babelfont --snap-component-transforms` changes the Back component to scale (-1,1) and translation (856,0). The Fore layer is correctly left alone. Moving the Refer to a `Layer: 2` "Sketch" layer gives the same result. FontForge would write that glyph as a simple glyph from Fore only, and it would never touch the other layers. The compiled TTF does not change, but a .glyphs or .babelfont output gets altered background and extra layers. The rustdoc ('Only a layer that FontForge's exporter writes as a TrueType composite') and the PR body sentence are false for such glyphs.
issues.fix: Skip every layer that is not a master's own layer, for example `if layer.is_background || !matches!(layer.master, LayerType::DefaultForMaster(_)) { continue; }`. The synthetic tests would then need a DefaultForMaster layer instead of `Layer::new`. At the least, skip `is_background` and say in the rustdoc, help and PR body which layers are touched. Add an SFD-driven test with a Back-layer Refer next to a Fore contour, and assert that the Back component keeps -0.999939/855.948/0.5.

issues.what: round_ties_even turns an offset in [-0.5, 0) into -0.0, and the Glyphs writer then writes a negative zero. I checked this with the HEAD binary: a Refer with offset -0.4, converted to .glyphs with --snap-component-transforms, gives `pos = (856,-0);`. FontForge's dumpcomposite stores the rint result in an int arg, so it writes 0. The test at :207-225 has no case in (-0.5, 0], so it does not catch this.
issues.fix: Normalise the sign after rounding, e.g. `t.translation.0.round_ties_even() + 0.0` (IEEE: -0.0 + 0.0 = +0.0), and do the same for .1. Add (-0.4, 0.0) to the rint test with an `is_sign_positive()` check.
